intro: Wisconsin runs its elections city by city, town by town and village by village, through each municipal clerk.

id_rule.text: Show an acceptable photo ID to vote at your polling place or to vote in person absentee at the clerk's office. Accepted IDs include a Wisconsin driver license or state ID card, a U.S. passport, a U.S. military ID, a Veterans Affairs ID, a tribal ID, or certain student IDs. If you vote absentee by mail, you send a photocopy of your ID, with some exceptions such as military and permanent overseas voters. A free state ID is available from the DMV.

check.text: Check your Wisconsin voter registration and find your polling place.
check.label: MyVote Wisconsin

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register online or by mail
dates.detail: Online and mailed registrations are due 20 days before the election. You must always show proof of residence when you register.

dates.label: In-person absentee voting
dates.detail: Clerks may begin in-person absentee voting 14 days before the election, and the last possible day is the Sunday before, Nov. 1. Each municipal clerk sets days, hours and places, so check with your clerk.

src.label: Wisconsin Elections Commission - in-person absentee voting

dates.label: Absentee ballot request deadline
dates.detail: Requests by mail, online, email or fax must reach your municipal clerk by 5 pm. You cannot take an absentee ballot out of the clerk's office if you ask for it in person.

src.label: Wisconsin Elections Commission - absentee request deadline

dates.label: Last day to register at the clerk's office
dates.detail: Register in person at your municipal clerk's office by 5 pm or close of business, whichever is later. After that you can still register at your polling place on Election Day with proof of residence.

src.label: Wisconsin Elections Commission - in-person registration deadline

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 8 pm. Absentee ballots must be in the hands of election officials by 8 pm, and a postmark does not count.

src.label: Wisconsin Elections Commission - absentee ballot delivery deadline
